questions.question: On 26 January 1950, the first ever Republic Day parade was performed at __ __.
questions.solution:

• The** inaugural Republic Day parade in India** was a small gathering. The solemn ceremony took place in the **nation's capital at the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium**, formerly known as the** Irwin Amphitheatre. **
 
• **Dr Rajendra Prasad**, India's first President, oversaw a ceremony to **raise the flag.**
 
• As the day the** Indian National Congress (INC) **issued the Declaration of** Indian Independence in 1930**, January 26 was chosen as India's Republic Day. The day was chosen since it was the day that the** Poorna Swaraj resolution of the Congress** was adopted.
 
• **Republic Day is observed nationwide** on January 26, 1950, the day the **Constitution became operative**. This day marked the beginning of India's ancient civilization, a mashup of **several cultures and kingdoms**. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Irwin Amphitheatre was the original name of the multipurpose stadium** when it was first built in 1933. Before the Asian Games in 1951, it was renamed National Stadium; Dhyan Chand's name was added in 2002. The Dhyan Chand Stadium hosted the** 2010 Hockey World Cup.**
 
• In 1950,** President Rajendra Prasad**, riding in a horse-drawn carriage, gets ready to march on the** first Republic Day parade on New Delhi's Irwin Amphitheater.** Republic Day commemorates the adoption of India's constitution and the country's conversion to a republic on **January 26, 1950.**
 
• On November 26, 1949,** the Constituent Assembly finished drafting the Constitution**. However, it was imposed on January 26th, 1950 to give the date, January 26th, the respect it deserved. Every year, we** commemorate this day by celebrating Republic Day. **

• **Nuruddin Muhammad Jahangir,** the Mughal emperor, regarded Kashmir as his favourite region in Mughal India.
 
• He was a naturalist, therefore **Kashmir's natural beauty** served as his inspiration and source of creativity.
 
• **Emperor Akbar visited Baramulla in 1580 AD** via Pakhil and stayed there for a short period of time.
 
• According to** "Tarikh-e-Hassan,"** the city was decked for Akbar's visit like a bride.
 
• When Jahangir visited Kashmir in 1620 AD, he also stopped in **Baramulla. ​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kashmir's history is entwined **with that of the larger Indian subcontinent as well as the bordering nations, which include Central Asia, South Asia, and** East Asia.**
 
• **The Kashmir region developed** into a significant Hindu and later Buddhist centre in the first half of the first millennium, under the Maurya and **Kushana dynasties.**
 
• A native **Shaivism tradition emerged later in the ninth century,** under the Karkota Dynasty.
 
• During the seven centuries of Hindu dominance, which continued under the **Utpala and Lohara kings** and ended in the middle of the fourteenth century, it prospered.

questions.question: Which of the following are the multi-purpose rock and earth-fill embankment dams on the Bhagirathi River?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Tehri Dam.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tehri Dam is the tallest dam in India.**
 
• It is India's largest hydroelectric power project, with a total planned installed** capacity of 2400 MW.**
 
• The** Tehri dam project was initiated by the government in 1969**. But it wasn't until 1990 that the government gave the Tehri Hydro Dam Corporation (THDC) the project to handle its restoration. 
 
• It is a** component of the Tehri Dam & Hydro Power Project,** a multi-use river valley project designed to take advantage of the River Bhagirathi's enormous potential for irrigation and hydropower. It is situated in **Uttarakhand's Tehri district.** Earth and rock are used to fill the **Tehri dam. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the** biggest dams in Maharashtra,** India, is the** Koyna Dam**. It is a dam made of concrete and rubble that was built on the Koyna River, which originates in **Mahabaleshwar, **a hill town in the **Sahyadri highlands**. It is situated on the state route between Chiplun and Karad in Koyna Nagar, Satara district, in the **Western Ghats.**
 
• On the** Ravi River,** which forms the border between the** Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir** and the state of Punjab, the Punjab Irrigation Department built the** Ranjit Sagar Dam, also known as the Thein Dam.** It is situated in Madhopur upstream of the Madhopur Barrage. 
 
• The** Gandhisagar Dam is located 168 kilometres **from the district office. The **Chambal River** is where the dam is being built. One of the four significant dams constructed on the **Chambal River in India is the Gandhi Sagar Dam. **The Madhya Pradesh state's Mandsaur districts are where the **dam is situated. **

questions.question: Vilasini Natyam and Veeranatyam are dances associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Andhra Pradesh.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **Indian classical dance style with its roots in Andhra Pradesh** is called **Vilasini Natyam.**
 
• Its repertory consists of female singer-dancers of **Telugu ancestry performing dance **operas, court dances, and temple dances.
 
• **Vilasini Natyam is the name given to the three-nrithya sampradayas**, or female dance tradition, of the Telugu Devadasis. Their repertoire included** ritualistic dances performed in temples **as described in the Agama sastras, ceremonial performances in courts, abhinaya-specific mezzuvani chamber concerts, and** Aata Bhagavatham natya** presentations.
 
• **Veeranatyam, also known as the Dance of the Brave **(Veera, which means brave, and Natyam, which means dance), is a traditional dance from the state of** Andhra Pradesh that has religious overtones.**
 
• In the beginning, **Veeranatyam was a rite conducted in Shiva** (Shaivite) temples as a tribute to Shiva. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This type of dance is most commonly performed by **Veerabhadra's devotees,** particularly the Veeramusti community in the state of **Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• Men perform Natyam, also known as** Veerabhadra Natyam,** in the East and West Godavari, Kurnool, Anantapur, and Khammam.
 
• The carrying of the** "Veerabhadra Pallem,"** a massive plate carried from the palms to the elbows and containing a camphor fire, is the first stage. Until the fire is put out, the dancing continues briskly to the beat of** multiple percussion instruments. **
